properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — Anthony, 2026-08-31, continuing the cleanup brainstorm after noting the `optimize` skill exists and has not been used much. Nothing chosen.

📌 DISTINCT FROM `dec:idea-should-optimize-be-a-served-skill-any-project-can-run`, having read it: that node asks WHETHER the skill should exist and be served, and its answer arrived by events — built, served, run twice. This node takes the skill's existence as given and asks what that one never raised: whether its SHAPE fits the work now proposed for it. A DEPENDS_ON edge to it is drawn deliberately.

THE TENSION, structural rather than a matter of taste. The skill is single-target in its own words: the title is "Optimise ONE thing, against a number you wrote down first", step 5 is "Change one thing", and step 6 stops the work the moment ONE budget is met. The proposed effort is the opposite shape — walk every subsystem, sweep for dead code, redundancy and slowness. A skill built to make work STOP is being asked to organise work defined by its breadth.

⭐ THE READING THAT DISSOLVES IT, and it stretches neither side: THE SWEEP IS STEP 1. Step 1 already says "measure where the time actually goes, then rank by COST PER UNIT OF WORK, not by total" — that IS a whole-codebase pass, and it is the only one of the seven meant to be broad. Steps 4-7 then apply to whatever the ranking tops, one target at a time, each with its own budget. On this reading the effort is not sweep-then-optimise-everything; it is ONE broad measurement followed by one or two bounded optimisations, and the skill already has the shape.

⚠️ WHAT THAT READING COSTS, stated because it is a real loss: step 1 ranks by cost per unit of work, which is NOT the ordering a subsystem walk produces, and a ranked pass never says when you are done. If what is wanted is assurance that every subsystem was looked at, step 1 does not supply it and nothing else in the skill does.

⚠️ AND STEP 1 EXPLICITLY PERMITS "NOTHING HERE": "A run that measures a set of tools and finds every one of them under a second is a SUCCESSFUL run of this skill. A version of this step that always finds something is a version that manufactures work." A sweep briefed as an elimination effort has a built-in pull the other way, and that sentence exists to resist exactly that pull.

📌 STEP 2 WOULD PICK A DIFFERENT TARGET than "each subsystem": measure the PRODUCT surface before the DEVELOPER surface. Of the three budget runs to date, two targeted the test suite and a structural read count; only the SPOF sweep touched what a user waits on. A third run has an obvious brief the skill itself would choose — what Alex waits on in a session.

OPEN SUB-QUESTION: does dead-code and redundancy work belong under `optimize` at all, or is that a different skill wearing a performance label? The skill measures time, memory and bytes; "code nobody calls" is none of those, and its sibling questions show the instruments for it are separately blind.
properties.name: OPEN — the optimize skill is single-target by construction and the proposed effort is a sweep; is the sweep step 1 of the skill, or does the skill need a shape it does not have?
properties.rationale:
Recorded under the brainstorm discipline. Raised because the mismatch is easy to miss: both the skill and the proposal are about "making things better", and nothing surfaces that one is a scalpel and the other a sweep until somebody tries to run one as the other.

📌 CREATED VIA `create_node` RATHER THAN `add_decision`, and the reason is itself a friction finding worth keeping: the near-match guard correctly refused twice and its remedy was to pass `related_to` — an array of relation OBJECTS — in the same call. This client serialised that argument as a string on both attempts ("invalid type: string ... expected a sequence"), so the prescribed route was not actionable from here. The judgement the guard was protecting was not skipped: `distinct_from` reasoning is stated above and the DEPENDS_ON edge was drawn immediately afterwards with `review_relations`. Note also that the served `add_decision` schema declares neither `related_to` nor `kind`, while the server accepts and requires them.
